implement: skill://legion-worker: the phase worker's whole contract — the shared workspace, the handoff write, the push with no skip-checks trailer on a code push, the pull request body from the template, and the implementer's own proof on a production-like surface at the head that merges.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the implementer writes the pull request body and its `E2E (implementer)` line and `proof` array; this change's proof is a daemon run, not a unit suite, so the definition of a proof and its negative control decide what may be written there.

skill://legion-worker/references/cleanup-deletion.md: the change deletes the boot's hand-written copy of the rule (`packages/daemon/internal/workflow/resume.go:145-155`), `closeAwaitingRoot`'s member scan (`linger.go:184-192`), two checkpoints of `scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh` and the `dispatch://LEGION-703` citation, so the deletion rules apply to each.
skill://legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: the implementer answers and resolves each review thread one by one after the reviewer's round, and is the only role that can resolve one.

skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md: the change touches `AGENTS.md`, the architect skill and the daemon's workflow package, all of which other live issue branches also touch, so a conflict or a retarget is likely and the forward-merge rule decides how it is brought in.
skill://ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass over the settled change before the implementer completes, which matters here because the rule is deliberately written once and read from four call sites.
test: skill://legion-worker: the tester's place in the gate, its own handoff, and the rule that it reads CI for everything static rather than running lint, types and the unit suites again.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the tester drives the changed surface for real, tries to break it, judges whether the implementer's tests would catch what it broke, and writes the `E2E (tester)` line and its `proof` array; the surface here is `bash scripts/e2e/merged-root-waits.sh` against a PostgreSQL and a `nats-server` the tester brings, plus the hand-run `legion state --json` readback.
skill://legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: the order of the gate the tester's verdict feeds, and what the tester's evidence must show before the reviewer reads the head.
review: skill://legion-worker: the reviewer's round — the read of the code commit's checks on GitHub, its handoff push, the review of the head that push made, then the completion.

skill://legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: the reviewer's submissions and its approval of a head by SHA, which READY later compares against; this change makes the gate itself the subject, so the reviewer reads the new acceptance refusal and the merged-root wait against the spec's check list.
skill://legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: one disposition reply per thread, never in bulk, and the bot threads the reviewer names to the implementer to resolve.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the reviewer verifies the other phases' proofs, which here means judging whether a daemon run driven through `daemon.run` rather than the shipped `legion start` is the proof the spec asked for — the plan's departure D1.

findings.finding: The spec prescribes one route to the real database the live proof needs — a workload in the cluster, `docs/kubernetes.md` 'Running a workload in the cluster from a role' — and pre-commits the implementer to reporting a blocker if it fails. That route is forbidden on the implementer's pod: `docs/kubernetes.md:2558` says 'Unless all three commands answer a bare `yes`, submit nothing', and the pod answers `kubectl auth can-i create jobs` = yes, `create services` = no, `get services` = no.
findings.answer: The plan's task 8 takes the database from the pod's own disk instead (the zonky embedded-postgres jar, the recipe `docs/solutions/testing/an-embedded-postgres-from-the-zonky-jar-runs-the-pods-postgres-lanes-and-the-nats-only-tests-are-skipped-by-name-LEGION-668.md` records), and the proof script hard-requires `LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN` and starts no database itself, so CI's service, a devbox container and the pod's jar all satisfy it and the tester can re-run it anywhere. I ran PostgreSQL 16.2 that way on this pod and the daemon's own suites passed against it. Recorded as departure D2; this is not a blocker.

findings.finding: 'the daemon's `legion state` report gains the pull request's state (`packages/daemon/internal/api/state.go:356`)' names one file. The field is a daemon API contract surface: `packages/daemon/internal/api/version.go` says a change to it bumps `DaemonAPIVersion` and the plugin manifest field in the same commit, the zod mirror is a `z.strictObject`, two goldens pin the wire shape, and the boot gate refuses a daemon whose number differs from the installed plugin's.
findings.answer: Task 3 makes it six edits in one commit: the Go field, the projection at `projection/project.go:143-150`, `legionPullRequestView` in `packages/contracts/src/legion-api.ts`, `DaemonAPIVersion` 35 to 36 with its numbered comment, `daemonApiVersion` in `packages/pi-legion/package.json` and `packages/claude-envoy/package.json`, and the regenerated `state.json` and `version.json` fixtures with the changelog entry contract 35 got. Check: `go test -count=1 ./internal/api/ ./internal/projection/` with no `-update`, then `bun test packages/contracts/`. The plan also names the consequence — a mismatch stops the implementer's own hand proof from booting.

findings.finding: 'One merge earns one notice' states an outcome with no mechanism. `closeMerged` is called from four places, two of which re-enter on every child departure (`closeAwaitingRoot`, whose caller `leave` runs on every issue leaving the workflow) and every daemon boot (`sweepMerged`), and notices never de-duplicate (`effects.go:160-165` writes a row per call). Placing the notice inside the rule would send one per child departure and one per restart, for days.
findings.answer: Task 2 has `closeMerged` report which issues it waited for, and only `merged` (`pullrequest.go:225`), the one path that records a new merge, writes the notice. `closeAwaitingRoot`, the boot sweep and `transition`'s already-merged branch write none. Two checks the spec's list does not carry are added: a second child leaving while a third still runs adds no `pr-merged` row, and a boot in that state adds none.

findings.finding: The downward walk's termination is unstated: a cycle in `issues.parent`, a parent recorded in another tree, a child whose parent is not recorded, and the walk's depth. The column is plain nullable text with no foreign key (`store/migrations/0004_record.up.sql:10`) and is rewritten from every Dispatch observation (`admit/admit.go:584`), so a human's re-parent lands in the record while `tree` stays as it was.
findings.answer: Task 1 states the three rules and points the implementer at the daemon's existing upward walk (`packages/daemon/internal/api/architect.go:688-713`), which already carries all three: a visited set so a cycle ends the walk rather than spinning inside the fact's transaction; only issues the tree lists are followed, so a parent in another tree is never reached; and an issue whose parent is empty or names a key the tree does not hold is beneath nothing.

findings.finding: The second half of the same finding: Rule 1 walks parents and Rule 2 reads the flat tree, so a member whose parent a human clears or re-points while it runs still holds the root's close but no longer holds the acceptance. Is that intended?
findings.answer: It is the spec's own design — it fixes Rule 1 on `issues.parent` read downward (and says the rule deadlocks read any other way) and Rule 2 on 'any other issue of its tree'. The plan implements both as written and records the consequence in its 'Decisions this plan makes' section rather than changing either.

findings.finding: 'When the last open child leaves the workflow, the existing `closeAwaitingRoot` closes the root' — so the wait ends only on a path that runs `leave`, its one caller. The spec never says what ends it when the last child stops holding the root another way, and a re-admitted child's `tree` is rewritten to its own key (`admit/admit.go:641-645`) with no workflow transition.
findings.answer: Task 7 requires the implementer to confirm the re-evaluation points and says why the named path cannot reach a waiting root: the orphan test runs only when the tree is not live (`admit/admit.go:544-559`), and a waiting root holds its admission slot, so `record.TreeLive` is true (`record/project.go:55-70`). Every remaining exit runs `leave`, and the boot's sweep is the backstop. If the implementer finds a path that leaves a member out of the workflow without running `leave`, task 7 requires it fixed here with a test, not deferred.

findings.finding: Two sentences give the already-merged shape two readings: the acceptance line says such a root 'waits the same way', and the change says an issue that reaches `awaiting_merge` on a pull request already merged 'was told at the merge itself and is told no second time'. The first reads as including the notice naming the children; the second forbids any notice there.
findings.answer: The plan reads them as the spec resolves them: 'waits the same way' governs the wait, and the notice sentence is specific to that case and governs the notice, so `transition`'s already-merged branch writes none. The cost — the architect of an early-merged root is not told which children hold its close, because the notice it already got names the pull request and the phase — is written into the plan's decisions and named to the architect, which is where an overrule belongs.

findings.finding: '`legion state` reports whether an issue's pull request is open, merged or closed' is in a list introduced as 'checked by a test that drives the daemon's workflow against a real database'. No workflow-engine test renders a state response: the wire shape is pinned by a Go golden and a TypeScript parse of the fixture, and the value is filled in a third package.
findings.answer: The plan gives that line its own surface in two places: the golden and the strict parse in task 3, and a readback of the live field in task 8 — step 2 of the proof asserts `pullRequest.state` is `merged` on the waiting root, and the hand-run `legion state --json | jq '.issues["<KEY>"].pullRequest'` on the shipped binary reads it once more.

findings.finding: The spec accounts for the eight tests the change invalidates and omits the one that covers the code it deletes: `TestTheBootSweepClosesMigratedMergedIssuesAndLeavesARootWithARunningChild` (`workflow/check_test.go:676`), while the spec also moves the log line that test's file sits beside.
findings.answer: Task 4 lists it as a ninth test, kept rather than rebuilt, with its assertions extended to the two facts the change moves: a boot that leaves a root waiting writes no 'closes' log line and no notice, and a boot that closes one writes the line.

findings.finding: 'both copies change unless the implementer finds the second is generated from the first' leaves a settled question open. `packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/` is generated: `packages/claude-envoy/AGENTS.md:50` says never edit it by hand, `scripts/build.ts:97-120` stages the files, and `check-dist` and `tests/legion-plugin-fresh.test.ts` fail on drift.
findings.answer: Task 5 names `skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md` and `skills/legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md` as the only sources and requires `bun run --cwd packages/claude-envoy build` to regenerate the mirror, with `bun run --cwd packages/claude-envoy check-dist` as the check. It saves the implementer a wrong edit that CI would refuse.

specDepartures.spec: The proof is a run of the `legion` process, the daemon booted on a real database, with each step read back from the daemon's own state.
specDepartures.plan: The two rules are proven on `daemon.run`, the function `legion start` itself calls, booted through the daemon package's whole-daemon harness in a driver built with the repository's `e2e` build tag; the shipped binary appears only in the hand-run `legion state --json` readback of the new pull-request state field. Facts still enter only by the transports production has, and every assertion is a read of the booted daemon's `GET /legion/v1/state` or of what it posted to Dispatch.
specDepartures.evidence: `packages/daemon/internal/daemon/daemon.go:191-193` (Run is run with zero overrides); `workflow.go:218-219` (no dispatch_url leaves the daemon with no workflow and no handlers, so neither rule can fire); `workflow.go:249-256` (with dispatch_url, boot reads both GitHub Apps' logins and mints an installation token per owner, which needs the Apps' private keys); `daemon.go:130-136` (the GitHub REST root is a test-only option with no command-line or environment knob). A worker pod holds App installation tokens for gh and git, never App private keys. The repository's own shape for this is `packages/daemon/internal/daemon/controller_sweep_live_test.go` with `scripts/e2e/controller-sweep-kind.sh`.

specDepartures.spec: The implementer gets the database as a workload in the cluster, under docs/kubernetes.md 'Running a workload in the cluster from a role'; something boot needs that cannot run where the work happens is a blocker to report.
specDepartures.plan: The database is an embedded PostgreSQL on the pod's own disk, and the proof script takes it as LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN and starts none itself. No blocker is reported, because everything the boot needs does run where the work happens.
specDepartures.evidence: `docs/kubernetes.md:2558` — 'Unless all three commands answer a bare `yes`, submit nothing' — against the pod's measured answers: `kubectl auth can-i create jobs` = yes, `create services` = no, `get services` = no. The pod route is recorded twice in this repository: docs/solutions/testing/an-embedded-postgres-from-the-zonky-jar-runs-the-pods-postgres-lanes-and-the-nats-only-tests-are-skipped-by-name-LEGION-668.md and docs/solutions/testing/the-pods-api-only-daemon-runs-no-outbox-lanes-a-tmux-stub-and-a-pgx-runner-boot-and-seed-it-for-a-state-proof-LEGION-694.md. I ran PostgreSQL 16.2 that way on this pod and the daemon's workflow and admit suites passed against it.

specDepartures.spec: The sequence to drive: the acceptance refused while the child runs, the parent's pull request merged by hand before the child is finished, the child's completion accepted, the child's merge, then the parent's acceptance taken and its close.
specDepartures.plan: The proof drives that sequence and adds a restart of the daemon while the merged root waits, before the child finally leaves.
specDepartures.evidence: Rule 1 refuses an acceptance while any child is in the workflow, so the spec's ordering reaches `awaiting_merge` only after the child is out, and `sweepMerged`'s behaviour at a waiting root — the code whose hand-written copy at `packages/daemon/internal/workflow/resume.go:145-155` this change deletes — is demonstrated by a boot at that state and by nothing else. The addition widens what is proven and narrows nothing.

specDepartures.spec: Silent on the NATS server, the Dispatch server and the workers the proof runs against.
specDepartures.plan: JetStream is a native nats-server pinned to the 2.10 line `packages/daemon/internal/testnats/nats.go:30` names, taken from LEGION_E2E_NATS_BIN or go-installed, rather than a container; Dispatch is the daemon package's own stand-in, extended to record what the daemon posts; the workers are the package's fake runtime. The driver's header says so, as the repository's other live proofs do.
specDepartures.evidence: `packages/daemon/internal/testnats/nats.go` is testcontainers over Docker and the pod has none; `scripts/e2e/stage3-4b13b-acceptance.sh:82` is the precedent for a native nats-server, and docs/solutions/testing/prove-a-nats-grant-in-a-docker-less-pod-by-rendering-it-from-the-branchs-own-code-INFRA-117.md the recipe. The real Dispatch server used by `startScratchDispatch` needs the `vector` extension the embedded PostgreSQL lacks (LEGION-668). `controller_sweep_live_test.go:1-14` and `burstable_live_test.go:1-13` are the form for declaring what a live proof stands in for.
